newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-INJURED SHEARER PROMISES WORLD CUP GOALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURED SHEARER PROMISES WORLD CUP GOALS.

text.p: Injured England striker Alan Shearer, who could be sidelined until the New Year, has pledged to return for club and country more deadly than ever.

"When I was lying in hospital recovering from my operation this week I made myself a couple of promises," the Newcastle player told the News of the World newspaper, who photographed him lying on a couch with his right leg in plaster.
"I'll be back for Newcastle for their bid to win something," Shearer declared.
"And I'll be raring to go for England next summer, when I intend to finish top of the goal charts at the World Cup finals, just as I did in Euro 96."
Shearer tore ligaments in his right ankle in the last minute of a pre-season friendly match against Chelsea last week and underwent an operation in Newcastle last Sunday.
The injury means the England captain will miss his country's World Cup qualifier against Moldova on September 10 and against Italy in Rome on October 11.
Shearer told the tabloid newspaper that he realised he would be out of action until early next year and said that he was not setting himself any specific target dates.
The paper said he had been told by doctors not to put any weight on his right leg for six weeks.
Despite the long layoff, he remained positive about the future and said his scoring targets were still achievable.
"Newcastle have a quality squad and will be up there challenging for the top honours by the time I'm fit to play again," he said in the interview.

"The same applies to England. There are plenty of good strikers capable of helping us qualify for the World Cup finals. But whoever replaces me must remember that he is only getting the number nine shirt on loan."
